messages:
incident-bot: Incident created: NET-4938 — Elevated p99 latency for hosted inference (us-west-2). Severity: P2. PagerDuty: Anjali Kaur.

Anjali Kaur: I'm on the page. Seeing p99 spike for text-gen endpoints across multiple models starting ~2026-03-15T13:02:00Z. Error rates for connections to upstream S3 artifacts also up.

Kyle Park: Confirmed. tcp retransmits & ECONNRESET seen in nodepool logs between us-west-2a <-> us-west-2b. Flow logs show intermittent packet drops. No config deploys from our side in the last 2 hours.

Maria Chen: Looping in AWS account team now. @AWS Support Bot please create a case with networking and NLB teams — this looks like inter-AZ network instability that may affect VIPs.

AWS Support Bot: Case created: 1234567890. Severity set to urgent. Initial contact ETA ~15m. Bridge scheduled: https://call.aws/bridge/awscase-1234567890 (confidential)

Nicole Reed: Quick ask from product — what customers are impacted? Any dedicated customers or private deployments in us-west-2? We need to know scope before sending notices.

Jake Moreno: Enterprise tenants with Dedicated capacity in us-west-2: AcmeCorp, BrightHealth, and LatticeOne. Several hosted API keys also see elevated latencies but not all. I'll pull a list and post shortly.

Anjali Kaur: Here are checks I'm running now (in order):
- verify NLB metrics in us-west-2 (Surge/TargetHealth)
- check k8s node networking counters + pod restarts
- confirm model artifact fetch latencies to S3
- run a small canary against inference pool in us-west-2c only

Kyle Park: Immediate mitigation attempt: routed traffic away from us-west-2a/2b to 2c via routing policy override and scaled up pool in 2c. Command used:

```bash
# bump up capacity in us-west-2c
kubectl scale deployment inference-pool-usw2c --replicas=12 -n inference
# pin routing policy
redwoodctl routes update --region us-west-2 --prefer-az us-west-2c
```

Kyle Park: Also disabled NLB cross-zone stickiness as a test (rolling back if it does not help).

Maria Chen: AWS response came back: "We're seeing internal packet loss in network spine in us-west-2 affecting some ELB frontends. NLB team is doing spine-level mitigation; we've requested a topology-level workaround for VIP rehoming." AWS provided ticket link and advised maintaining bridge.

Anjali Kaur: Customer-facing status page draft (please review, we may need legal/CS edits):

```
Summary: We are currently investigating elevated request latencies for hosted inference in the us-west-2 region. Customers may experience slower responses or request timeouts.
What we're doing: We have routed traffic to healthy availability zones and engaged the cloud provider for an infrastructure-level investigation. Mitigations in progress may temporarily alter routing to reduce impact.
Impact: Customers with workloads in us-west-2 may see increased latency or errors. Dedicated and private deployments in the region may also be affected.
ETA: Monitoring for stability; we will provide updates every 30 minutes or when we have new information.
```

Jake Moreno: CS suggested targeted email for Dedicated customers. Draft snippet below (please edit):

```
Subject: Service disruption affecting Redwood Inference in us-west-2 (ongoing)

Hi <CustomerName>,

We're investigating elevated latency impacting inference endpoints in the us-west-2 region. Our engineering team has implemented routing changes to minimize impact and is working with our cloud provider (AWS) on a root cause. If you rely on Dedicated capacity in us-west-2, our team will keep you updated via this thread and direct email.

Estimated next update: in 30 minutes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is critical and appreciate your patience.

— The Redwood Inference Reliability Team
```

Nicole Reed: +1 to transparency, but remove the line about "root cause" until AWS confirms. Say "investigating with cloud provider." Also include a link to status page.

Anjali Kaur: Noted. Updated status and email template posted.

Maria Chen: For vendor coordination: AWS has assigned a TAM (L. Singh) and created a dedicated engagement channel. They asked for packet captures and NLB config dumps. Kyle, can you grab tcpdump on one of the affected nodes and sanitize?

Kyle Park: On it. Will collect captures from edge nodes and upload to AWS case. Command I'm running:

```bash
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/usw2-spine-capture.pcap host <elb-ip> and port 443
# will scp to secure bucket and share link with aws
```

Anjali Kaur: Handoff plan: I'm going to stabilize routing and keep bridge open for 30m. Maria, can you take primary ownership on the vendor bridge for the next shift? I'll leave detailed notes in the PD incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-98765

Maria Chen: Taking handoff. I'll keep AWS engaged and chase NLB team for VIP rehoming. Next on-call: @pagerduty please escalate to Kyle Park if primary bridge loses connectivity.

pagerduty: Handoff recorded. New primary: Maria Chen. Secondary: Kyle Park. Escalation rules applied.

Anjali Kaur: Quick internal ops checklist I added to incident:
- bridge up
- AWS case id pinned (1234567890)
- captures uploaded to secure share (link below once done)
- status page + targeted emails queued
- monitor p99 and error rate dashboards every 5m

Kyle Park: Uploaded sanitized pcap and NLB config to case: https://s3.redwood.internal/cases/1234567890/payloads/pcap-sanitized.pcap (AWS has access). Logged AWS response: "VIP rehoming in progress; expected behavior change in 10-20 minutes."

Maria Chen: Thanks. I'll keep pushing for a concrete ETA and update status page when AWS confirms stable. If VIP rehoming doesn't clear within 30m, we'll consider cross-region fallback for critical enterprise tenants.

Nicole Reed: Please flag if we need to spin up cross-region capacity and coordinate comms. CS standing by for outbound notices.

incident-bot: Update: AWS reported partial mitigation at 2026-03-15T13:21:00Z — observed improved packet loss metrics on spine. Request latencies trending down; monitoring.

Anjali Kaur: Good progress. I'm marking the incident as "mitigated" in PD but keeping it active until we're stable for 60m. Leaving detailed log in the incident timeline and handing final updates to Maria.

Maria Chen: Will post follow-ups and an RCA draft after AWS provides root cause. Closing vendor coordination loop here for now; will reopen thread if AWS provides further action items.

Jake Moreno: CS will send targeted customer updates once you confirm final wording. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Nicole Reed: Thanks team — nice tight coordination.

[end of thread]
